advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid double cross-session detection on the MCP path — reuse the field-computed advisory rather than re-detecting inside the suppressed instrumented library call.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:45: `return cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=None)`
src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py:39: `state = show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` and :41 `config = load_config(repo_root)`
src/rebar/_lib_warn.py:55: `msg = cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` invoked from the instrumented mutator (e.g. src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:333).
advisory.finding: On the MCP write/read surfaces the cross-session advisory is detected twice per operation: _mcp_writes._cross_session calls cross_session_warning_for (which reads the ticket via show_ticket + load_config), and the now-instrumented underlying library call (e.g. transition/comment) independently calls emit_cross_session_warning which repeats the same detection before it is suppressed by the global filter.
scenarios: Every MCP single-ticket write/read now performs an extra show_ticket read + config load whose result is discarded (warning suppressed).

evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:599: `    _warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=_CrossSessionWarning)`

build_server() is invoked ~100 times across tests/ and by the CLI entrypoint (search for 'build_server(' — many tests call it in-process), so the global filter is installed by ordinary construction, not only in a dedicated server process
The filter is unqualified (no message/module scoping) and there is no matching teardown/reset, so it persists for the process lifetime and mutates state shared with rebar library callers
advisory.finding: build_server() installs a process-global, unqualified warnings filter `filterwarnings("ignore", category=CrossSessionWarning)` as a side effect of constructing a server object, and never removes it. Because build_server() is called throughout the codebase/tests in-process, this permanently mutates the global warnings state for the whole process, suppressing CrossSessionWarning for unrelated library callers (and defeating tests that assert emission after any build_server call).

only test_cross_session_cli.py:148 `assert res.stderr.count(_HOLDER_MSG) == 1` (link path)

advisory.suggested_fix: Change the show/comment/transition CLI cross-session assertions from `in` to `== 1` count, matching test_link_warns_for_primary_endpoint_only.

This is a global, permanent mutation of the interpreter warning filters rather than a scoped/context-managed suppression like the CLI's suppress_cross_session_warning().
blocking.finding: build_server() installs a process-wide warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=CrossSessionWarning) as a permanent side effect that is never removed; in any process where the MCP server is built and library API (`import rebar`) callers also run, all CrossSessionWarnings are silently swallowed globally, not just for MCP-originated calls.
scenarios: An embedding process constructs the MCP server and also uses `rebar.show_ticket`/mutators directly — those library calls no longer surface CrossSessionWarning.
Repeated build_server() calls prepend duplicate ignore filters.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no CLI handler runs instrumented library mutators on a spawned thread, or propagate the suppress context (copy_context) so the guard holds across handler threads.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_warn.py:16: `_EMITTING: contextvars.ContextVar[bool] = contextvars.ContextVar(...)`
src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py:63: `with suppress_cross_session_warning():` wraps `_invoke` which runs the handler on the current context only.
ContextVar values are copied to a new thread only when the thread is started with a copied context (e.g. via copy_context().run); a bare threading.Thread starts with default (False).
dropped.finding: The CLI re-entrancy/suppress guard uses a contextvars.ContextVar, which does not propagate to threads a handler may spawn; if a CLI handler dispatches library mutators on a worker thread, the suppress_cross_session_warning() guard set on the main thread will not apply there, allowing a duplicate stdlib CrossSessionWarning alongside the CLI's own WARN line.
scenarios: A CLI command whose handler offloads library calls to a thread pool would double-warn.

scenarios: Running a single-ticket CLI command (e.g. `rebar comment <A-held-tid> "x"`) as session B while ticket is in_progress held by session A: contract requires exactly one advisory (the CLI WARN line) with no leaked stdlib CrossSessionWarning.
